solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Engaging in local tour, turned ahead to progress slowly in Crosby?

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so this short word is read backwards

parts.note: a side that is ahead in a match is said to be one up

indicators.note: the verb for moving slowly sits inside the singer's first name

parts.note: to move at a snail's pace

explanation.surface: Someone taking a leisurely tour of the area around Crosby, Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: PU goes ahead of B(CRAWL)ING to give PUB-CRAWLING. Crosby looks like the Liverpool suburb but is the singer Bing.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a British neighbourhood pub, so touring several of them in one evening is pub-crawling.

clue.text: Leading vehicle has to compete with top retracted

indicators.note: drawn back, so the combined words are read from the end towards the start

parts.note: to compete in a contest of speed
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A car that leads must race with its roof folded back.
explanation.walkthrough: RACE CAP read backwards gives PACE CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The pace car leads the field of a motor race on formation laps or behind a safety caution.

clue.text: Potential trouble coming from deranged relatives son supports

indicators.note: in a down entry, a letter that supports others sits underneath them, at the bottom

explanation.surface: Family trouble from mad relatives whom a son props up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping on fruit peel is the comic emblem of a pitfall, so these are hazards waiting to trip someone up.

clue.text: God is here ultimately to provide uplift

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A deity is present to give spiritual lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up, giving it elevation.

clue.text: Whale epithet also adapted for this football chant?

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling someone a whale is the sort of insult British football crowds turn into a chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who ate all the pies?' is the terrace taunt British football fans sing at an overweight player or referee, which is what 'whale' already implies.
explanation.definitionFit: This mocking question is a well-known song sung by fans in stadiums at portly opponents.

clue.text: The writer's regret about old city's corrupt constituent

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and I'm is I am

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for regret wraps round the ancient city

explanation.surface: A writer laments the corrupting element found in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: An impurity is a contaminating element, something within a substance that spoils or debases it.

clue.text: Draws line under reason for basic principles

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed below, so the reason word comes on top

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for divorce
to rule a line is to draw it with a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone underlining a justification to set out fundamental ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground rules are the basic agreed principles under which an activity or discussion proceeds.

clue.text: Here one may find shops are opened by scoundrel

indicators.note: something opened up has an item put into its middle, so the villain splits this word

explanation.surface: Shops that are opened by a rogue, as if a crook ran the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopping arcade is a covered walkway lined with retail outlets.

clue.text: Gather tea's brought up in the morning

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means moved to the top, and what moves is the abbreviation for the morning

parts.note: Assam is a variety of Indian tea; its last two letters are the morning abbreviation

explanation.surface: Gathering together for an early morning cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The AM at the end of ASSAM is lifted to the top of the down entry, giving AM + ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate things into a pile or quantity.

clue.text: Demand huge amount to power our planet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: idiom for asking an exorbitant price
second meaning, whimsical: put electrical charge into the world

explanation.walkthrough: The second half takes the idiom literally, as if charging a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to ask an extortionate price, while literally it would mean supplying the world with electricity.

clue.text: Style shown by Labour's leader in European city

parts.note: to dub is to name or style someone

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so just the opening letter of the party name counts

explanation.surface: A party leader displays fashion sense in a continental capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of the Republic of Ireland, in Europe.

clue.text: Swedish-American star almost in dress

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian film star nearly appearing in costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially of a distinctive kind, as dress is.

clue.text: Jogger encountered on the Champs-Elysees?

parts.note: surface reading: a runner met on the famous Paris avenue
setter's reading: a memory jogger, named in the language spoken along that avenue

explanation.walkthrough: Jogger means a prompt to the memory, not a runner; the Paris setting says the term is French.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing literally means help to memory: a note or object that prompts recall.

clue.text: Regressive boy wrecked last old reformatory

indicators.note: going backwards, so the short boy's name is read in reverse
something wrecked is broken up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A delinquent lad who wrecked things last ended up in a reform school.
explanation.definitionFit: A borstal was a British detention institution for young offenders, abolished in 1982.

clue.text: One going aloft in ship under the wind

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means placed beneath, so the vessel comes second

explanation.surface: Someone climbing the rigging of a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going aloft' suggests a sailor climbing the mast, but it is something that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: An airliner is a large passenger aeroplane, which goes up into the sky.

clue.text: Principal director brings in northern chap to make money abroad

indicators.note: to bring in is to admit inside, so the boss takes the other parts into the middle

explanation.surface: A company chief hires a man from the north to earn money overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The centimo is a small coin, a hundredth of the currency unit in Spain formerly and several Latin American countries.

clue.text: Men, splitting apart, strangely maintaining correspondence

indicators.note: splitting means cutting into, so the soldiers go inside the other letters
strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of apart are disordered

explanation.surface: Men living apart who oddly still keep up a correspondence by letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Correspondence here means proportion, not letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro rata means in proportion, keeping a share that corresponds to each part.

clue.text: Spectacular performance where learner breaks cover

indicators.note: breaking into something means entering it, so the novice letter goes inside

parts.note: a folder or cover holding loose papers
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A dazzling show in which a trainee blows someone's cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' looks like the definition-adjacent BLIND, but the L goes into BINDER.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a blinder is an outstanding display, as when a player has a superb game.

clue.text: Endeavour by arrangement to have superb small pianos

parts.note: to concert is to plan or strive together by agreement

explanation.surface: An effort to acquire some excellent compact pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small pianos' sounds like uprights; S joins the adjective, and the pianos are the largest kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Concert grands are the largest grand pianos, built for recital halls.

clue.text: Diver in vehicle test on craft circling lake

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the test follows
circling means going all round, so the cunning word surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: A scuba diver in a boat goes round a lake for a safety check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat but means cunning; 'Diver' is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The guillemot is a seabird of the auk family that dives underwater to catch fish.

clue.text: Republican, accompanied by venomous types, speaks hoarsely

explanation.surface: A politician surrounded by poisonous colleagues talks in a croaky voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To rasp is to utter words in a harsh, grating voice.

clue.text: Almost endure consuming American spread

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so the shortened verb takes the country inside
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the verb goes

explanation.surface: Barely putting up with a big American meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFER loses its R, then SUFF(US)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffuse is to spread through or over something, as colour or light does.

clue.text: Fuel the very thing needed in an ancient Balkan location

indicators.note: something needed in a place goes inside it, so the pronoun sits within the region name

parts.note: Thrace, the ancient region of the south-east Balkans
as in 'that's it', exactly what is wanted

explanation.surface: Fuel is just what is wanted in some old Balkan settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is hard, slow-burning coal used for heating.

clue.text: A bit of a laugh with one in credit control meeting

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the abbreviation for the money term

explanation.surface: A joke at a dull meeting about credit control.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to preside over it and keep it in order.

clue.text: Brutish sort, throwing back thin plate

indicators.note: throwing back sends it the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a lamina is a thin layer or plate

explanation.surface: A thuggish type hurls back a flimsy dinner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an animal says they behave like a beast, crudely and violently.

clue.text: Worker at lodge stores wood and food

parts.note: a porter staffs a college or hotel lodge

explanation.surface: A lodge porter keeps timber and provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse steak is a thick cut of beef, a substantial dish.

clue.text: Artist in decline — could depression cause this?

explanation.surface: A painter in a slump, wondering whether depression is the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression is meteorological, a low-pressure system, not low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather lows bring clouds and wet weather, so precipitation is what they typically produce.

clue.text: Novel touching and useless because without chapter

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the shortened conjunction goes round the abbreviation
read as use-less, the conjunction is to be without those three letters

explanation.surface: A moving story that is pointless because it lacks a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: BECAUSE minus USE leaves BECA, which goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's 1938 Gothic novel set at Manderley.

clue.text: Man's excellent knowledge about British regiment in border area

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the learning word wraps the regiment and preposition

parts.note: Al's, belonging to a man called Al

explanation.surface: A soldier's expert knowledge of a regiment posted in a frontier zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace-Lorraine is the region on the Franco-German border long fought over by the two countries.

clue.text: Too much here to be taken out of context — remember?

indicators.note: taking something out of a passage lifts consecutive letters straight from it

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A complaint about a quotation being taken out of context, asking someone to recall it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface warns about quoting out of context, which is exactly the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means going far beyond what is reasonable or moderate, which is excessive.

clue.text: Trouble with heart? Here's comfort in retirement!

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
British slang: bottle is nerve or courage, as is heart

explanation.surface: Someone with heart problems finds solace after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' looks medical but means courage; 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber container of heated liquid warms a bed, a comfort when someone retires for the night.

clue.text: Element turning stomach in clergyman losing work

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the shortened churchman
losing means going without, so the clergyman sheds the word for work
turning round makes the informal word for belly read backwards

explanation.surface: A vicar feels sick on being made redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: Op is short for opus, a numbered musical work; tum is informal British for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismuth is a heavy metallic chemical element, number 83.

clue.text: Likely to notice retainer having departed?

parts.note: obiit, Latin for 'died', as on gravestones
a retainer is a household servant

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed servant who has left service.
explanation.walkthrough: The departed retainer is read as a dead one: OB, then SERVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An observant person is quick to perceive and take note of things.

clue.text: Lived in luxury endlessly in Datchet's outskirts

indicators.note: in places the shortened adverb between the town's edge letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of the town are used

parts.note: first and last letters of Datchet

indicators.note: endlessly means with no end, so the final letter of the adverb goes

parts.note: living in luxury is living well

explanation.surface: Someone lived lavishly on the edge of Datchet, a well-to-do Berkshire village.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to live or reside somewhere.

clue.text: Loss expert acting as receiver for chemical company

indicators.note: a receiver takes things in, so the skilful word holds the company inside

parts.note: Imperial Chemical Industries, formerly a major British firm

explanation.surface: A bankruptcy specialist appointed receiver for a chemical firm that lost money.
explanation.walkthrough: Receiver suggests insolvency, matching 'Loss', but here it just means holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is a shortfall, the amount by which spending exceeds income.

clue.text: Try hard to catch glimpse of Romeo — stick around

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the stick word goes round the code letter

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone straining to see Romeo while waiting with a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To crane is to stretch the neck to see something better.

clue.text: Admitting nothing in crash, I paid out for the other driver

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the zero is put among the fodder letters
out means disordered, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist admits no fault after a collision but pays the other driver anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is a British euphemism for sex, so 'the other driver' is something that drives desire.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac stimulates sexual desire, so it drives one towards sex.

clue.text: Vessel having rope at bow in tangle

indicators.note: a tangle is a mess, so these letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat with its mooring line knotted up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerboat is a fast motor-driven craft, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Large American trucks transporting new phones

indicators.note: trucks transporting a load carry it inside, so the abbreviation goes within

explanation.surface: Big American lorries hauling a delivery of new telephones.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British usage for calling them on the telephone.

clue.text: Cautious taking dangerous bends

parts.note: on as in on medication, taking it

indicators.note: bends means twists, so the letters of the adjective are contorted

explanation.surface: A careful driver negotiating hazardous bends in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's guard means staying alert and wary, ready for danger.

clue.text: Exile concerned with stale atmosphere vacated enclosure

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: first and last letters of enclosure

explanation.surface: An outcast stuck in a stuffy, abandoned compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone who has fled their homeland, displaced like an exile.

clue.text: Serious in backing learned person to become an idol

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so this short word is written backwards

parts.note: a mage is a learned man or magus

explanation.surface: A solemn scholar backed to become a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A graven image is a carved figure worshipped as a god, which the Bible forbids.

clue.text: Nurse working after pains located around sick body part

indicators.note: after means following, so the nursing words come at the end
around means encircling, so the pains word goes round the illness word

explanation.surface: A nurse on duty treats painful symptoms in a patient's body.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscles to the heel bone.

clue.text: No sailor alights on isle

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means resting on top, so the verb sits above the island

parts.note: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A landlubber arrives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A landsman is a person who lives on land and has no seafaring experience.

clue.text: Secret meeting with Tory and Liberal inside underground chamber

indicators.note: inside means within, so the party letter is placed in the chamber word

parts.note: a cave is an underground chamber

explanation.surface: Tories and Liberals meet clandestinely in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclave is a private meeting, notably the closed gathering of cardinals electing a pope.

clue.text: Mountain pass on ring road constructed in state

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means sitting above, so the pass comes first

parts.note: a col is a pass between peaks

indicators.note: constructed means built up, so these letters are put together in another order

parts.note: a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: A mountain route built onto a ring road in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the Spanish word for reddish, it is one of the fifty American states, in the Rockies.

clue.text: Have riches perhaps in a vault

parts.note: a vault is a leap, as is a bound

explanation.surface: Someone wealthy keeps riches in a bank vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like a strongroom for riches, but it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to be plentiful, and having riches is one example of having plenty.

clue.text: Add to men relieving us in some 31 days?

indicators.note: relieving means taking over a post from someone, so one group replaces the other

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be replaced

explanation.surface: Soldiers relieve a unit for a month's posting to boost numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: In AUGUST the US is swapped for MEN. 'Some' with the question mark signals one month among several with 31 days.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to increase something by adding to it.

clue.text: Doing well in Duke of Milan's university

indicators.note: in places the college abbreviation within the possessive name, before its final letter

parts.note: Prospero's: in The Tempest, Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan

explanation.surface: Success at an Italian aristocrat's university.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means thriving financially, flourishing and successful.

clue.text: Saw things in Société Ethnologique?

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the French society's name

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second, accents dropped

explanation.surface: Someone saw curious objects at a French ethnological society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see; it is the cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The cutting points along a saw blade are called its teeth.

clue.text: Society girl pursuing house party organiser

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so these pieces come after the house abbreviation

explanation.surface: A debutante chasing a house party.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostess is a woman who receives and entertains guests at a gathering.

clue.text: Belong essentially out there? On the contrary!

indicators.note: on the contrary asks for the opposite, so each word is swapped for its antonym

explanation.surface: Asking whether something truly belongs outside, then insisting the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist as a permanent, intrinsic quality within something.

clue.text: Musical flourish modified signals at party

indicators.note: modified means changed, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician changes cues at a celebration with a flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a series of notes, an ornamental musical effect.

clue.text: Happy home deity to constrain old ghosts

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold in, so the deity keeps the ancient letter inside

explanation.surface: A household god restrains some ancient spooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good spirits means being cheerful and in a positive mood.

clue.text: Children that may be taken where there's disagreement?

definitions.text: that may be taken where there's disagreement?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the idiom to take exception to something

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint at the phrase 'take issue with'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means offspring in legal language, and is the noun in the idiom for disputing a point.

clue.text: Absurd and mad to toss away shilling

indicators.note: tossing something away discards it, so the coin letter is removed

parts.note: s was the abbreviation for the shilling, an old British coin worth a twentieth of a pound

explanation.surface: Crazy to throw money away.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, lacking sense or meaning.

clue.text: European move abroad to unseat good foreign government

indicators.note: to unseat is to remove from position, so the letter for good is thrown out

parts.note: to migrate is to move to another country

explanation.surface: A European emigrates to topple a decent overseas regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf.

clue.text: Barker grabbing little Mexican food

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of, so the dog takes the small word inside

parts.note: the tosa is a Japanese breed of fighting dog
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A dog snatching a bit of Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a crisp fried tortilla topped with beans, meat or cheese.

clue.text: Eastern sea creature shedding tail in Spring

indicators.note: shedding a tail means losing the end, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: An oriental sea cow losing its tail in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' is a verb, as in spring from a source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or originate from a source, just as things spring from somewhere.

clue.text: Cosmetic procedure for legendary friar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: surgery that tightens skin, as in a tummy one
second meaning: the jovial friar of Robin Hood's band

explanation.surface: A medieval monk booked in for plastic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic surgeons perform a tummy version, and Robin Hood's portly companion bears the name.

clue.text: Strict at all times in case of sabotage

indicators.note: in places the time phrase inside the shell letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of sabotage

explanation.surface: A tough stance always taken when sabotage is suspected.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh and stern, imposing rigorous standards.

clue.text: Closer minders so upset with order to protect stronghold

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the jumble goes round the fortress word
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the fodder words are jumbled

parts.note: a keep is a castle's central tower

explanation.surface: Supervisors closer to a stronghold restoring order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' is something that closes, a door, not an adjective meaning nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doorkeepers guard doors, which are things that close, so they mind closers.
